Lawrence was inspired to reflect upon death and myths of resurrection when writing the first part of *The Escaped Cock* after a visit to some Etruscan tombs with his friend Earl Brewster. This trip encouraged him to contemplate themes related to death and resurrection, which became central to the first part of the novel. The experience likely influenced the novel's exploration of mortality, the afterlife, and the symbolic significance of the "escaped cock" as a metaphor for these themes.

inputs.context: The Escaped Cock is a short novel by D. H. Lawrence that he originally wrote in two parts and published in 1929. Lawrence wrote the first part in 1927 after visiting some Etruscan tombs with his friend Earl Brewster, a trip that encouraged the author to reflect upon death and myths of resurrection. "The original short story version of Part I of the novel appeared in The Forum magazine, February 1928." Lawrence added the second part in 1928 during a stay in Gstaad, Switzerland.
